summary: In Greek mythology, Eteoneus (Ancient Greek: Ἐτεωνεύς) was one of the twenty-three suitors of Penelope who came from Same on Cephallenia — a namesake of Eteoneus son of Boethous, Menelaus' busy squire at Sparta in the Odyssey.

sections.heading: Suitor from Same
paragraphs: Apollodorus' Epitome lists Eteoneus among the wooers from Same, named after Thriasus and before Clytius in the island catalogue. With the other suitors he was killed when Odysseus returned, aided by Eumaeus, Philoetius, and Telemachus.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (eteoneus-same) is the Same suitor of Penelope. Distinct from Eteoneus son of Boethous, the Lacedaemonian weapon-carrier and herald of Menelaus who met Telemachus at the Spartan gate and kindled the fire at his master's bidding — the better-known Homeric figure of the same name.
